title: Issi ben Yehudah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Sometimes [called] Issi without further designation, or Issi ben Gamliel, or ben Mahalalel, or Issi ben Akiva – Akavya, or Yosef of Hutzal – Yosef the Babylonian.

Hyman regards the Sages’ words as undoubtedly true and right in Pesachim 113b: “It was taught: Yosef of Hutzal is Yosef the Babylonian, is Issi ben Gur Aryeh, is Issi ben Yehudah, is Issi ben Gamliel (Dikdukei Soferim: ben Gamla), is Issi ben Mahalalel; and what is his name? Issi ben Akavya is his name.” Hyman considers it very likely, as the author of Seder HaDorot holds, that because of the persecution he changed his name and his father’s name. When you examine his names they are not so many, since Issi and Yosef are almost one; he was from Babylonia, from the town of Hutzal; Yehudah is Gur Aryeh (explicitly in Vayechi, 49:9: “Yehudah is a lion’s cub”); and they called him ben Mahalalel because he enumerated the praises of the sages. Hyman also regards it as clear that his father is not the well-known Rabbi Yehudah without further designation, for in Gittin 67a Issi ben Yehudah said, “Rabbi Yehudah is wise when he wishes”; had he been his father, he would not have said so. Likewise he regards it as clear that he was not the son of Rabbi Akiva, since he considers that a scribal error and proposes ben Akavya; he also said of him, “Rabbi Akiva is a sealed storehouse.” Hyman insists that Issi lived two generations after Rabbi Akiva.

notes.text: All name forms, including Akiva/Akavya and DikdukeiSoferim Gamla, are retained. Hyman’s emphatic undoubtedly, clear and two-generation chronology remain attributed rather than weakened or silently harmonized; the compressed final sentence is rendered as his stated reason.

The consulted Pesachim 113b directly lists Yosef of Hutzal, Yosef the Babylonian, Issi ben Gur Aryeh, Yehudah, Gamliel, Mahalalel and Akavya. Hyman’s emphatic acceptance, persecution explanation, father-name arguments and two-generation chronology are preserved as his conclusions; the selected list does not independently prove those reconstructions or the exact Dikdukei Soferim Gamla reading.
